title: Leaderboard by Custom Score
statement:
A group of `N` friends play a video game. Friends are numbered from `1` to `N`, and friend `i` has won `A[i]` matches and lost `B[i]` matches.

The score of friend `i` is `(A[i] - B[i])^2 / (A[i] * B[i])`, computed exactly as a fraction (not rounded). The leaderboard lists the friends from the **highest score to the lowest**. If two friends have the same score, the one with the **higher number** (the one who played later) ranks better.

Print the friend numbers in leaderboard order.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `N`.
Each of the next `N` lines contains two integers `A[i]` and `B[i]`.
outputFormat: Print `N` lines: the friend numbers from the best rank to the worst, one per line.

examples.explanation: The scores are 1/2 for friend 1, 1/6 for friend 2 and 4/8 = 1/2 for friend 3. Friends 1 and 3 tie, and friend 3 has the higher number, so the order is 3, 1, 2.
The scores are 0, 9/4, 9/4 and 1/2. Friends 2 and 3 tie at 9/4 and friend 3 wins the tie, then friend 4 (1/2), then friend 1 (0).

hints: Sort by score descending, and by friend number descending when scores are equal.
Floating-point division can make two equal scores compare as different. Compare two fractions p1/q1 and p2/q2 by cross-multiplying: p1 * q2 versus p2 * q1.
With A, B ≤ 5000, the numerator and the denominator are at most 25,000,000, so the cross products stay below 10^15 and fit in 64-bit integers.
